page: Microsoft Azure E4ds_v4 is an Intel-based virtual machine belonging to the EDSv4 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. This instance features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon 8272CL cores with hyper-threading enabled. Operating at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz, the processor includes 35 MB of L3 cache and supports instruction set extensions such as AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI. The hardware configuration is memory-optimized, delivering 32.0 GB of RAM, which equates to a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Additionally, the server includes 154 GB of local SSD storage and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance tradeoff between the server's high memory capacity and its processing throughput. The CPU performance is generally limited, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core tests, PassMark CPU scores, and Geekbench multi-core results all falling into the bottom 25% of benchmarked servers. Memory bandwidth also registers in the lower tier, with uncached read speeds at 27.67 GB/sec and write speeds at 21.69 GB/sec. However, single-threaded operations show moderate efficiency, as evidenced by average-tier scores in Geekbench single-core execution, text processing, and gzip compression.

Given its hardware profile, the E4ds_v4 offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require a larger memory footprint without demanding intensive parallel CPU processing. The 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it suitable for hosting small-to-medium relational databases, caching layers, and memory-bound enterprise applications. The inclusion of 154 GB of local storage supports temporary database tables and caching files, though the weak multi-threaded decompression and database operation benchmarks suggest it is less suited for heavy, write-intensive transactional databases or high-throughput web serving.
